forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: East Devon auditors need separate strategy to restore confidence in council accounts
news_drafts.lead: External auditors have told East Devon's Audit and Governance Committee they need a formal strategy to regain assurance over the council's financial statements. The committee will receive a separate regaining assurance strategy and capacity assessment alongside the external audit progress report. The development reflects wider strain on audit capacity: Grant Thornton's fee for auditing the council in 2025-26 has been set at £169,103, reflecting "increased work auditors must now undertake as well as the scarcity of audit firms willing to do this work." Planning delays occurred in July and August 2026 because of officer capacity to respond to audit queries, though auditors report being in a good position for the critical post-statement audit phase beginning in mid-September.
news_drafts.paper_title: External Audit Progress and Sector Update 2025-26

news_drafts.headline: East Devon faces permanent £3.8m budget deficit as government cuts funding
news_drafts.lead: East Devon Council faces permanent budget deficits of £3.861m in 2027/28 and £4.722m in 2028/29, driven by government decisions to cut funding allocations. These are not temporary pressures but permanent reductions in the money available to the council. The council plans to use reserves — money set aside — of between £2.7m and £3.9m to close the 2027/28 gap. However, the council's own financial strategy identifies that "the key risk is that short-term balancing decisions in 2027/28 create a structural problem for 2028/29 and beyond." The planned savings meant to prevent this remain limited. Planning fee reforms are expected to deliver £1.4m but are prudently assumed at £0.5m pending legislation due at year-end; a leisure contract renegotiation may deliver at least £0.5m.

news_drafts.headline: East Devon faces £3.8m budget deficit driven by permanent loss of government funding
news_drafts.lead: East Devon faces a structural budget deficit of £3.861m in 2027/28 and £4.722m in 2028/29, driven by permanent reductions in government funding including business rate rebasing and the ending of New Homes Bonus. The Cabinet has acknowledged the council's financial position has "fundamentally changed through external factors beyond the Council's control." To balance its budget, the council plans to draw down £2.7m to £3.9m from reserves in 2027/28, alongside an additional £3m in reserve requests. However, the financial strategy explicitly warns that "the key risk is that short-term balancing decisions in 2027/28 create a structural problem for 2028/29 and beyond." Identified savings plans — including planning fee reform and leisure service negotiations — are uncertain and dependent on external legislative and contractual decisions, falling significantly short of the deficits being forecast.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Plan Progress Report - Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: Council Maintains Zero Overdue Audit Actions Despite 70 Open Items
findings.detail: As of 25 August 2026, the council has no overdue Priority 1 or Priority 2 actions. 11 actions have been closed since 1 July 2026, demonstrating that management is maintaining remediation momentum.
findings.matters: Keeping actions on schedule demonstrates management responsiveness and effective execution on audit remediation, mitigating the impact of outstanding control weaknesses.
findings.figures: 0 overdue actions against 70 open total; 11 actions closed since 1 July 2026
findings.quote: As of 25 August 2026, the Council has no overdue actions. 11 actions have been closed since 1 July 2026.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Plan Progress Report - Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: Information Governance and Performance Management Limited Audits Remain Unresolved After 2+ Years
findings.detail: Both 2023/24 Limited assurance audits continue unresolved: Information Governance (4 open), Performance Management (4 open). This suggests ongoing management execution or resource constraints in addressing identified control weaknesses.
findings.matters: Multi-year persistence of unresolved audit findings indicates systemic management effectiveness issues and may constrain the council's ability to deliver corporate priorities and meet compliance obligations.
findings.figures: Information Governance: 4 open of 13 total; Performance Management: 4 open of 7 total
findings.quote: Information Governance Policies and Compliance with Retention Policy Limited 2023/24 4 0 5 4 13 and Performance Management Limited 2023/24 4 0 2 1 7

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Plan Progress Report - Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: Contract Management Limited Assurance Audit Has 7 Open Actions; Area Now Designated Strategic Risk
findings.detail: The 2025/26 Limited assurance audit identified significant procurement control gaps. 7 of 10 agreed actions remain open as of 25 August 2026. Contract management has been added as a new strategic risk (Gov 26) on the council's risk register.
findings.matters: Contract management is core to procurement control; persistent open actions expose the council to supplier management and procurement risk.
findings.figures: 7 open actions out of 10 total from 2025/26 audit

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Plan Progress Report - Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: Disrepair Claims Audit Completed with Limited Assurance and 8 Priority 2 Actions
findings.detail: A new audit of disrepair claims management was completed in Q1 2026/27 with Limited assurance opinion, generating 9 agreed actions including 8 Priority 2 ('important findings that need to be resolved by management').
findings.matters: Disrepair claims represent potential landlord negligence liability; Priority 2 actions indicate important findings requiring management resolution and potentially costly remediation.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Plan Progress Report - Quarter 1 2026-27
findings.headline: Housing Legionella Compliance – 12 Open Actions Remain Unresolved
findings.detail: The 2025/26 Limited assurance audit identified significant control gaps in legionella management. As of 25 August 2026, 12 actions remain open. A follow-up audit has been prioritized for 2026/27 with actions due to be completed in-year.
findings.matters: Legionella management is a statutory safety obligation; 12 open actions from a Limited assurance opinion represent material compliance exposure with potential liability implications.
